sentences.text: Ciridops was an extinct genus of honeycreepers that once inhabited the Hawaiian islands of Hawaii, Molokai, Kauai, and Oahu.
These birds featured a strong bill with an arched culmen, a term for the ridge on the upper jaw that overlapped the lower jaw at the base.
Additionally, the nostrils of these birds were covered by a membrane.
They possessed large wings and a moderate tail with pointed feathers.
The genus was established in 1892 by Alfred Newton based on the ʻula-ʻai-hawane, originally named Fringilla anna by Sanford B. Dole in 1879.
The ʻula-ʻai-hawane was the only species observed in historic times until it was last seen in 1892.
The genus belongs to the family Fringillidae and the subfamily Carduelinae.
Researchers suggest that the nearest relatives of Ciridops might have been from the genus Loxops.
The genus lived during the Late Pleistocene, between 0.129 and 0.0117 million years ago.
